§5.7 Layout Regions

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

layout-layout-regions · rule layout

✅ Normative

A region's class MUST be settled before its content is rendered, because the class decides which rule governs the rendering. A region rendered under the wrong class is non-conforming however faithfully its text is transcribed.

A producer segments each page into regions, each carrying a label. The label decides which rule applies — so getting the region right is upstream of every other decision in this protocol.

This note maps the vocabulary that region detectors commonly emit onto the protocol. The protocol's own classes, and what box each gets, are defined in Block Classes§5.3 and Block Annotation§5.1. Detector labels MUST be resolved to those classes before they become layout annotations. The resulting layout class MUST match the corresponding Markdown element's class in Elements§3.1.

The vocabulary

Structure title · doc_title · section-header · paragraph_title · text · content · abstract · list-item · document-index

Data table · chart · formula · formula_number · code · algorithm · number

Figures picture · image · figure_title · caption

Forms form · key-value-region · checkbox-selected · checkbox-unselected

Page furniture header · page-header · footer · page-footer · footnote · aside_text · reference · reference_content · seal

The label decides the rule

Label Governing rule
table Is This Even a Table§9.1.5 and the whole Tables chapter
chart Cover Every Data Point§11.1.1
picture / image Images and Figures§12.1.2
form / key-value-region The Key-Value List§10.3.2
list-item Bullets and Sub-Bullets§8.1
caption / figure_title Titles Banners Captions§9.7.3
formula Displayed Equations§7.2.2 — LaTeX in $$ … $$
checkbox-* Checkboxes§10.4.2

A detected label is evidence, not a verdict

A region labelled table is not automatically a table. Address blocks, two-column prose and ungridded specification stacks are routinely labelled table by layout detection, and Is This Even a Table§9.1.5 exists to overrule that. A detected label MUST NOT be accepted on its own: the region MUST be classed by what is actually printed.

The same holds in reverse: a genuine grid that detection missed MUST still be rendered as a table.
